sources.citation: Parakh, Mona. 2019. Preliminary Phonological Description of Rathvi. Language in India 19(4): 266-275.
sources.note: Not this language (Rathvi of Chhota Udepur = rath1243). Sec. 6.1: stress pattern 'not dealt with in this work'. Listed only to record that the nearest published Bhil phonology sketch is also silent on stress placement.

sources.citation: Varkey, Vinod Wilson & Kishore Kumar Vunnamatla. 2018. A Sociolinguistic Study of Bareli/Pauri and Related Languages. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2018-011. Dallas: SIL International. 197 pp. [Glottolog 582125]
sources.note: The only modern source on Palya (sec. 1.2.1 'Palyas'; Palya wordlists Choutharya + Natvada, RTT/SRT at Choutharya). Sociolinguistic only: no phonology chapter; Appendix C p. 74 (p. 81): 'the wordlist data as well as transcribed texts included in subsequent appendices are field transcriptions and have not undergone thorough phonological and grammatical analysis'. 'Stress'/'accent' appear only in the sociolinguistic sense. Silent on word stress.

sources.citation: Lewis, M. Paul, Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2016. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 19th ed., entry 'Bareli, Palya' [bpx] (Internet Archive copy 2016-08-18); and Ethnologue 2025 free view of the same entry (Internet Archive copy 2025-03-04).
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: no phonology content: the 19th-ed. entry has population, location, status 6a, classification, dialects/lexical similarity, language use, literacy, religion - no Typology field and no bibliography; the 2025 free view adds only 'NT (2020)'. Closes the 'current Ethnologue edition might cite a phonology write-up' works still to obtain: it does not.

sources.citation: Ethnologue 17th ed. (2014), entry 'Bareli, Palya' [bpx] (open edition, Internet Archive copy 2014-08-09); also Ethnologue 15 (2005) snapshot
sources.note: Identity only: alt. names Pali, Palodi; 10,000 (2000 V. Varkey); dialect centre Choutharya village, Rajpur tahsil; lexical similarity 62-66% with Pauri Bareli, 67-73% with Rathwi Bareli; no bibliography beyond OLAC. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Grierson, G. A. (ed.). 1907. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. IX Part III: The Bhil languages. Calcutta. Sections 'Bhili of Ali Rajpur and Barwani' (pp. 61-62) and 'Bhilali of Barwani' (p. 67)
sources.note: Only pre-modern coverage of the Barwani Bhil dialects (Palya not named; 'Palya/Pali/Palodi' absent from the volume). Pronunciation notes are segmental only (broad a, palatals, v>b, cerebral l, -lo suffix). The only 'accent' lines in the volume are the front-matter transcription convention (acute accent, illustrated with Khowar). Nothing on stress.
